title: Traceable integration-point field recovery
summary: Preserves raw constitutive integration-point fields in a partition-independent HDF5 scientific source and converts them to separately named weighted DG0 visualization fields without nodal extrapolation, interelement smoothing, or material-boundary averaging.

science.statement: A scientific cell field is the quadrature-weighted mean of one constitutive integration-point field over each element; its processing history is part of the result meaning.

equations.label: weighted cell recovery
equations.description: Reference-cell quadrature weights form one DG0 value per cell; no neighbor contributes.

inputs.name: quadrature field
inputs.description: Point coordinates, weights, constitutive values, value shape, and owning mesh.

outputs.name: recovered field
outputs.type: FieldResult carrying a DG0 Function and processing metadata
outputs.description: A compact cell field suitable for quantitative queries and point/cell visualization.

outputs.name: raw integration-point dataset
outputs.description: Partition-independent physical-cell IDs, point coordinates, physical weights, reference rule, raw values, and field semantics readable without DOLFINx.

assumptions: The quadrature rule and stored values describe the same reference-cell point order.
DG0 is a cell-average representation and does not retain within-cell variation.
conventions: Raw integration-point fields keep their original names; recovered variants use an explicit *_CELL suffix in J2 and creep SimulationResult objects.
J2, creep, viscoelastic, learned-material, and finite-strain J2 result paths retain raw quadrature fields with an explicit sampling contract.
solve_result(output=...) writes recovered cell fields to XDMF/HDF5 and raw values to a separate *.integration-points.h5 scientific source.
Material boundaries are preserved because recovery is performed independently within every cell.
A smooth contour is a later presentation product and never overwrites constitutive evidence.
applicability: J2 plasticity and implicit creep field inspection, ParaView cell contours, histories, extrema, and learning-data preparation with explicit processing semantics.
limitations: The compact writer currently gathers owned rows on rank zero; independently partitioned extreme-scale output remains a later performance route.
Material-domain nodal extrapolation and smoothing are not yet implemented.
For curved non-affine cells, a physical-Jacobian-weighted recovery will need a distinct reviewed policy.

validation_rules: Reject sources without explicit quadrature points and weights.
Sort owned rows by stable original physical-cell identity and reject duplicates.
Verify serial and two-rank archives preserve physical weights, coordinates, and raw values.
Reject policies that silently request a non-DG0 or cross-material recovery.
Check weighted values independently and preserve processing metadata in SimulationResult.

references.title: Abaqus integration-point output and extrapolation semantics
